items.section: For people with red-green color blindness,

items.text: always make sure the visual difference between the default state and the focus state is recognizable.
Note: If you want to remove the default :focus styles but still show focus indicators for keyboard users, you can use the :focus-visible CSS pseudo-class.
Always test your forms on different platforms,
You must also make sure to validate data before storing or sharing it on your backend server: find out more.
You also need to specify which fields are mandatory.
items.section: Why should you validate your forms?

items.text: Make sure all users understand your validation rules.
However, to communicate error or success you should never rely only on color.
The :user-invalid pseudo-class solves this issue, as the styles are only applied after user interaction.
Use smaller text sizes for smaller screens and larger text sizes for larger screens.
It's important that you don't use the vw by itself in a font-size declaration.
Don't set your line-lengths with a fixed unit like px.
Use a relative unit like rem or ch.
Use unitless values for your line-height declarations.
Use @font-face to tell browsers where to find your web font files.
Use woff2 as your web font format.
Use the CSS font-display property to tell the browser how to manage the switchover from a system font to a web font.
Use a font-display value of swap if you still want the web font to replace the system font whenever the web font finally loads.
Use a font-display value of fallback if you want to stick with the system font once text has been rendered.
You probably don't want your text to shrink and grow to extremes.
